note: Title VII / ADA compensatory + punitive damages caps under 42 U.S.C. 1981a(b)(3), by employer size. These caps apply ONLY to compensatory (non-pecuniary, e.g. emotional distress) + punitive damages combined. Back pay and front pay are NOT subject to these caps — back pay is equitable relief under Title VII itself, and front pay was held uncapped by the Supreme Court in Pollard v. E.I. du Pont de Nemours & Co., 532 U.S. 843 (2001). Caps are fixed at 1991 levels and have never been indexed for inflation. Punitive damages are unavailable against public/government employers (42 U.S.C. 1981a(b)(1)). ADEA claims (age discrimination) use a wholly different remedy structure: back pay + liquidated damages (a doubling of back pay for willful violations) — no compensatory/punitive caps apply because none are available under the ADEA at all. California FEHA claims have NO statutory cap on compensatory or punitive damages.
